posts.title: Xiaomi Auto signs first German dealers, paving way for 2027 European sales
posts.summary:
Xiaomi Auto signed MoUs with an initial group of 8 German automotive dealer groups and will enter the European market in 2027.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Xiaomi Auto has signed Memoranda of Understanding with eight German dealer groups, establishing the foundation for its planned European market entry in 2027.
The move signals a strategic shift toward a traditional dealership model for international expansion, leveraging local partners with expertise in premium automotive sales and service.
While specific models and pricing remain undisclosed, the company is accelerating its international infrastructure, supported by its existing R&D center in Munich.

posts.title: Chery-JLR launches Freelander 8 in China below pre-sales price, targeting luxury EREV SUV market
posts.summary:
The Freelander 8 starts at 289,900 yuan ($42,750) after incentives and has a CLTC battery-only range of 310 km.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: The Freelander 8 marks the revival of the brand through a Chery-JLR joint venture, entering the competitive luxury EREV SUV segment with a starting price of 289,900 yuan.
The vehicle features an 800-volt 6C platform capable of 20% to 80% charging in 12 minutes, paired with a 60.3-kWh CATL battery providing 310 km of CLTC range.
Standard equipment includes Huawei's Qiankun ADS 5 driver-assistance system, dual-motor AWD, and a high-performance powertrain delivering 610 kW and 813 Nm of torque.

posts.title: Scaling agentic AI pilots across the enterprise
posts.summary: As agentic AI moves from experimentation toward enterprise deployment, the challenge is figuring out how agents can work together, connect to the systems and data they need, and operate safely across the workflows that run a business. Although agentic AI has been adopted by some 80% of Fortune 500 companies, progress toward meaningful scale remains…
bullets: While 80% of Fortune 500 companies have adopted agentic AI, most remain stuck in isolated pilot phases rather than achieving enterprise-wide integration.
Successful scaling requires moving beyond experimentation to align AI deployment with specific financial objectives, such as cost reduction or revenue growth.
Organizations must avoid layering AI onto inefficient legacy workflows, instead redesigning processes to leverage the autonomous capabilities of agentic systems.
Effective deployment necessitates treating AI agents as part of the workforce, requiring robust governance, security, and the ability for agents to access unified data and back-end systems.

posts.title: AI Is Forcing Data Centers To Rethink Trust
posts.summary:
Exploding compute demand is exposing new gaps across the hardware supply chain, from chip identity and firmware integrity to post-quantum readiness.
The post AI Is Forcing Data Centers To Rethink Trust appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Data center security is shifting from traditional perimeter controls to a 'zero trust' model that requires verifiable evidence for every component in the supply chain.
Hyperscale facilities are increasingly vulnerable to remote physical attacks and supply chain compromises, leading some operators to scrap entire server shipments due to unverified logistics.
Cryptographic agility and component provenance tracking are becoming mandatory requirements for modern data centers to mitigate risks associated with AI-driven threats.

posts.title: AI, tools and transformation
posts.summary:
It’s very tempting to imagine that AI turns everyone into a tool-builder - 
now everyone can just ask the model to make the software they need, and 
apps as we know them are dead.  I think that misunderstands how most people 
think and where software actually comes from, and more importantly, it 
isn’t a path to change how companies actually work.
bullets: Large enterprises currently suffer from 'software sprawl,' managing thousands of disparate systems, SaaS applications, and shadow IT workflows that often go unmonitored.

While AI lowers the barrier to building automation tools, the assumption that software will become entirely dynamic and spontaneous ignores the reality that most employees are not natural 'tool-builders.'
Domain experts, such as lawyers or salespeople, focus on their core professional responsibilities rather than identifying or architecting software-based efficiencies.
The true value of AI in the enterprise may rely on 'forward-deployed engineers' who bridge the gap between technical capabilities and the unarticulated needs of non-technical staff.
